-92.97980,44.91760.name: Reproductive Medicine & Infertility Associates
-92.97980,44.91760.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Jacques P. Stassart, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-82.42000,23.11800.name: Centro de Ingeniería Genética y Biotecnología
-82.42000,23.11800.desc: Cuba’s state genetic engineering centre, which developed and manufactured its own COVID vaccines and exports biotechnology products. A small embargoed country built a vaccine industry from public investment, which is the sharpest available counter-argument to the claim that only private capital can do this work.

-77.04420,38.90780.name: Revolving door records
-77.04420,38.90780.state: Washington DC — OpenSecrets revolving door database
-77.04420,38.90780.desc: Tracks people who moved between a regulator and the industry it regulates, in both directions, from public filings. It matters here for a specific reason: the decisions on this map are made by small committees in small fields where the people qualified to assess an application are frequently the people who have worked on one. That is not itself wrongdoing, and it is the sort of thing a reader is entitled to know before weighing an assessment.

-47.06000,-22.90600.name: TEVAH Consulting
-47.06000,-22.90600.desc: The regulatory-consulting facet of this map holds fourteen records, twelve of them in North America and Europe, which reads as though dossier work is done only where the biggest regulators sit. Brazil approves more engineered organisms than almost anywhere, and this is one of the firms that prepares the submissions. Its listed services describe the whole apparatus a Brazilian applicant must satisfy: biosafety manuals, training for the in-house biosafety commission each institution must maintain, the annual biosafety inspections CTNBio requires, commercial dossiers and their submission, following the file in Brasília, answering requests for further information, and registration with the agriculture ministry, the environment institute and the health agency as applicable. It also develops PCR and ELISA detection kits — the same firm that writes the dossier can supply the test for what it describes. Its consultants are described as drawn from academic institutions and the agricultural biotechnology industry.
